official.deadline_note: KIIT's own international admissions portal publishes no KUISP closing date for the current round - it states only 'Admissions 2026-27 Open Now, Only for NRI & Foreign Nationals'. The most recent KIIT-authored KUISP leaflet (2025-26 cycle) published 'Application Start Date: 1st March 2025' and 'Application Deadline: 30th August 2025', and KIIT asked Indian missions to recommend students by 30 September 2025. No dated 2026-27 deadline is confirmed on any official awarding-body page.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 admissions round (KUISP itself is announced per academic year; the 2025-26 cycle ran 1 March 2025 to 30 August 2025)
official.status_note: KIIT's international portal states 'Admissions 2026-27 Open Now - Only for NRI & Foreign Nationals', and KIIT's Scholarships & Fellowships page lists 'International Scholarships - 100' as currently available.
official.tuition_coverage_note: KIIT's Scholarships & Fellowships page states: 'KIIT International Scholarship - Two students and ten students from each country are provided with full and half tuition fee waivers respectively. A total of 100 scholarships are available.' The KUISP leaflet states '50% to 100% scholarship on Tuition fees for the whole course duration'. KIIT's own fee page publishes the pre-waiver international tuition of USD 10,000 per annum for undergraduate and postgraduate courses and USD 4,000 per annum for PhD (USD 8,000 for UG/PG SAARC).
benefits: 50% to 100% scholarship on tuition fees for the whole course duration
Examination and registration fees for the whole course duration
eligibility: KUISP is applicable to foreign national applicants for undergraduate, postgraduate and doctorate programmes, and also to short-term training programmes
Applicants with good academic standing in their home institutions are encouraged to apply
Applicants should have a valid passport
Applicants should fulfil the course eligibility criteria as per university norms

Undergraduate: passed grade 10 and grade 12 or equivalent; Postgraduate: passed secondary/higher secondary and a bachelor's degree in any discipline; Doctorate: passed postgraduation in any discipline

PhD full-time applicants must engage as full-time research scholars on campus for a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 5 years; part-time applicants must be working full time in a private organisation, corporate, government department, school or university in their own country
KIIT asks Indian diplomatic missions to recommend a maximum of ten students from their country of accreditation
requirements: Application must be submitted through the KIIT International Admission Portal at https://international.kiit.ac.in or sent by email to internationaloffice@kiit.ac.in

Applicants must register, verify their registered email via the link from kiit.global@kiit.ac.in, complete the programme and personal details, address, educational qualifications and upload sections, then submit the declaration

documents: Copies of secondary/higher secondary education transcripts and certificates
Copy of bachelor's degree transcripts and certificate (postgraduate applicants)
Copy of master's degree transcripts and certificate (doctorate applicants)
Recommendation letters (postgraduate and doctorate); recommendation letters or a letter of interest within 250 words for doctorate
Copies of certificates of academic honours or awards received (if available)
selection_criteria: KIIT publishes 100 international scholarships in total, with two students per country receiving full and ten students per country receiving half tuition fee waivers
Good academic standing in the home institution
Fulfilment of the course eligibility criteria as per university norms
KIIT states that the quantum of scholarship and the period of scholarship are subject to change from time to time
coverage: 50% to 100% scholarship on tuition fees for the whole course duration
Examination and registration fees for the whole course duration
application_method: Register and apply online at the KIIT International Admission Portal, https://international.kiit.ac.in
Alternatively send the application by email to internationaloffice@kiit.ac.in
Applications may also be routed through the recommendation of an Indian diplomatic mission, limited to a maximum of ten students per country of accreditation
official.application_route: Apply free of charge through the KIIT International Admission Portal (international.kiit.ac.in) or email the International Relations Office, with optional mission recommendation.
official.study_mode: Regular mode, English medium; PhD offered both full-time (minimum 3, maximum 5 years on campus) and part-time
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign national applicants only; Indian missions may recommend a maximum of ten students from their country of accreditation
official.international_eligibility: Yes - KUISP is a scheme for foreign national (international) applicants only and is not available to Indian nationals
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: KUISP is offered for courses in the schools named in its annexures: School of Language (BA/MA English), School of Social, Financial & Human Sciences (BA/MA Economics, Sociology, Psychology, BCom/MCom), School of Mass Communication (BCJ/MCJ) and School of Film & Media Sciences (BFTP), plus PhD specialisations in computer, civil, electrical, electronics and mechanical engineering, applied sciences, biotechnology, languages, mass communication, social/financial/human sciences, sports & yogic sciences, public health, management and rural management, and law
official.research_requirement: Doctorate applicants must submit recommendation letters or a letter of interest within 250 words
official.duration: The whole course duration: KUISP lists 4-year undergraduate, 2-year postgraduate and 3-5 year PhD programmes
official.description: KIIT Deemed University announces the KIIT University India Scholarship Program (KUISP), applicable to foreign national applicants to pursue professional education in India at KIIT-DU, for regular undergraduate, postgraduate and doctorate programmes and for short-term training programmes.
official.program_type: Institutional tuition-fee scholarship for international students across undergraduate, postgraduate, doctoral and short-term training programmes
official.english_requirement: Basic English language proficiency (beginner level); proof of English proficiency such as TOEFL or IELTS is requested if the applicant has any, and KIIT's admissions guidance notes this is not compulsory. Applicants from non-English-speaking countries must submit English-translated documents.

verification.notes: Award value, benefits, eligibility and documents were confirmed from KIIT's own Scholarships & Fellowships page, its international fee and eligibility pages on the KIITEE admissions portal, and the KIIT-authored KUISP leaflet distributed through Indian missions (hcipretoria.gov.in, June 2025). KIIT publishes KUISP as a percentage tuition waiver, not as a currency sum, so funding_amount is null. No closed date for the 2026-27 cycle is published on any KIIT-owned page; a 2026 Algerian Ministry of Higher Education notice recirculating KIIT's offer gives 30 October 2026 for the 2026/2027 round at master's and PhD level, but that is a third-party page and not the awarding body, so it is treated as unconfirmed.

applicant_utility.summary: KUISP is a tuition-fee-only award: KIIT waives 50-100% of tuition for foreign nationals, but you still pay for hostel, food, airfare, visa and insurance. The scheme is capped at 100 scholarships worldwide with only two full waivers per country, so it is competitive even though the application is free. It is offered across listed humanities, social science, media, law, management and engineering/PhD schools rather than KIIT's full course list, and KIIT publishes no closing date, so apply as early as possible once the portal opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funded-at-heart international applicants who can cover accommodation, food and travel themselves but need tuition relief, especially those from countries with a large applicant pool and strong school grades.
application_readiness_checklist: Check that your intended programme sits in a school named in the KUISP annexure (language, social/financial/human sciences, mass communication, film and media, or the listed PhD specialisations) before starting an application
Register on international.kiit.ac.in, verify the email link from kiit.global@kiit.ac.in, and complete every stage of the form to get an application number
Scan your passport, school leaving certificate, and full secondary/higher-secondary transcripts plus bachelor's and (for PhD) master's transcripts
Obtain recommendation letters and, for doctorate, a 250-word letter of interest
Get every non-English document officially translated into English
Budget roughly USD 500 one-time registration plus about USD 2,000 per year for AC three-sharing hostel and four daily meals, which the leaflet states students pay themselves
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a programme outside the KUISP-eligible schools, such as B.Tech, MBBS, BDS or B.Arch, which are not covered by the scheme
Losing out on a per-country slot because only two full and ten half waivers exist per country inside a worldwide cap of 100 scholarships
Submitting incomplete transcripts that stop at the last degree instead of tracing secondary education
Assuming a mission recommendation substitutes for a complete portal application, or waiting for a mission route that has already closed
PhD part-time applicants who are not actually employed full time, which contradicts the published part-time criterion
Missing English translations of certificates from a non-English-medium school
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The KUISP leaflet states the scholarship does not cover airfare tickets, visa fees, medical insurance, stipends, personal living expenses or a laptop. Students additionally pay a one-time registration fee of USD 500 and an annual fee of USD 2,000 covering AC three-sharing hostel accommodation and four meals a day (vegetarian plus non-vegetarian).
document_audit: The passport must be valid for the whole study period, and a scanned copy is mandatory
The school leaving certificate is requested separately from transcripts
Proof of English proficiency is 'if any', so do not wait for an IELTS result, but translated transcripts are effectively compulsory for non-English schools
Doctorate applicants need either recommendation letters or a 250-word letter of interest, a stricter limit than most KIIT PhD routes
Awards/honours certificates are optional but are the only published way to evidence merit beyond grades
alerts: KIIT's own site states admissions for 2026-27 are open but publishes no KUISP closing date; treat the window as short and apply on day one
The previous KUISP cycle ran 1 March to 30 August with missions recommending by 30 September, so an early-year portal registration matches the historic pattern

A separate scheme, the KIIT International Semester Scholarship Programme, also exists for one to two semesters with publication fees of USD 500 plus USD 1,250 per semester - do not confuse it with KUISP

Earlier KUISP leaflets excluded SAARC countries and KIIT's fee schedule still prices SAARC applicants separately at USD 8,000 per annum, so confirm whether your nationality falls inside the current round
KIIT explicitly warns that the quantum, eligibility and duration of the scholarship can change, so verify against the latest notification before committing
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the KIIT International Admissions Portal, verify your email, complete the programme, personal, address, qualification and upload sections, submit the declaration to receive an application number, then wait for the offer letter in your student dashboard.
